utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, just for myself, what was just read to you is the leadership have broadcasted message to the public, that the army will continue fighting, and then it reads, "however, the RSK Supreme Defence Council decided about the evacuation." You can read this in several ways. Apparently Mr. Misetic did read it and I'm seeking your confirmation that that is the right reading that the evacuation was also part of the message that was broadcasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The evacuation message was part of the broadcast and it contained -- it concerned civilian and elderly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was also -- that is not unambiguous on paper, therefore, I was seeking clarification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Section 4: "Trains are seen being moved in Knin. Comment: Presumably used for military purpose but could these be used for the evacuation of civilians?" First, did you see the trains moving in Knin?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many times during the day -- or let me ask it a different way. At what point in the day did you see trains moving?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed that from UN Sector South headquarters so that would have been in the afternoon when we had evacuated there. And we did that around 3.00 or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now you said presumably used for military purpose. What did you presume that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been used to move forces. But it was in the end, I think, abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they realised that the railroads were not the best option for moving either civilians or military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, that very report, if I could take you back to section 2. On the radio -- I gather from the statement on the radio it was said that the evacuation is to the territory of Republika Srpska. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evacuation was through RSK territory and it also had a final destination in Belgrade, perhaps also, but that is also to RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, I'm looking at the portion that says: "Decided the evacuation to RS."

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right. So that's -- you heard in the radio message that the evacuation had been decided to the RS or the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, either it had the -- either I had heard it in a background as being translated to me, or that it was brought to us by fellow monitors. This is the RC Knin report and I was the operation officer, so I'm compiling the information at that time. Some of it not being my own observations. It is an important distinction between that and the team reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if I could have again 1D50-0001. This is the diary again. I'm sorry, D741. And if we could go please to -- I only have the D numbers on the bottom, so it would be 0062. I'm sorry, I have the wrong document on the screen. Madam Registrar, it is 1D50-0202.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this is your notebook that I'm going it bring up, Mr. Liborius. Do you recognise that as the cover page of the notebook we were looking at this morning -- or this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could go to 1D50-0238, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, much of this is also in Danish. So I would ask you to please translate this for us. I assume the Babel Fish online translator that helped me translate portions of this is that it's titled, Urgent report to DAN DEL.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I have the date prior -- oh, sorry, yes, I have it here, yeah. Say again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it titled, Urgent Report to DAN DEL?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could you translate that for us?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Foreign language spoken] Monthly report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Monthly report, okay. And then if you -- could you translate line by line what it says?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Monthly report to DAN DEL. Input regarding Operation Storm in Sector South and in circled text out to the left about RSK. [Foreign language spoken] The way things passed. RSK collapse. Fleeing. Military RSK. RS help. Caught by their own propaganda. Village population, situation as refugees now. Then there's a circle CRO, Croatia. Quickly in. Totally planned operation. Underline problematic questions. POWs, civilians, non-POWs. The tactic of the scorched earth in a new form. Cattle, farms, why, an arrow, psy-ops, motivation or grounds, revenge (ethnic cleansing). A circled text RS, spillover: Psy-ops. Rivalry, political rivalry. Supplies, or lack of supplies, [Foreign language spoken] indicates lack of. Basic recipe for collapse, stricken out, and another word for collapse [Foreign language spoken] in Danish. And then the rest of the page there's a [Foreign language spoken] --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there's a what?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Foreign language spoken] future, abbreviation for future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, who -- was this something that was dictated to you or were these your own thoughts?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My own thoughts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm interested in the sentence that -- on the RSK caught by their own propaganda. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RSK had a much overinflated belief, I think, in their own military compatibilities. Secondly, their abilities to get constant support from RS and the Belgrade government. A belief that led them to not properly interpret and assess the situation during the peace negotiations that were conducted. And that led them to, apparently up through the summer of 1995, believe that their capabilities were far greater than they in fact were. And that their propaganda about rejecting any cooperation, future relations with the state of Croatia that they possessed such resources that they could just reject that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, just for future reference, and your answer is fine, I'm just -- I'm reminded to tell that you I will pause after your answers. There will probably be a long pause so I can allow the court reporters and the translators to finish, so if there is an silence in the room it is not because I'm expecting you to continue to answer. It has happened with other witnesses before. You wouldn't be the first to think that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender the entire notebook into evidence, we've had the discussion before and we will have a discussion about the translation of the entire notebook and I again will be referring back and forth to various dates in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the notebook would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D743.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm reminded to clarify for Madam Registrar and the Court that we received it in two different parts from the OTP, presumably because it is a such a large file, and therefore I would ask that somehow we include the entire notebook even though right now it is separated in e-court. It is two exhibit. And the other Exhibit is 1D50-0080.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, is there a possibility to have the two -- we are still talking about this notebook in two portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. It's just divided, I think, around October 23rd, if I'm not mistaken, and then continues on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, is there a possibility to reunite the several parts of the notebook, electronically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think we may want to use two numbers because until that is done I'm going to be referring to both portions today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D743 is the portion of the notebook that has been brought up on the screen. Do you want to tender the other part right away? Yes. And that would be -- you have given, I think, already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that second portion of the notebook would be exhibit number ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The second document will be Exhibit D744, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, I take it that there are no objections either. D744 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Madam Registrar, if I could have -- this was on the Prosecution's list of exhibits, so I think it is going to get a P number at some point, but I will call it up by the 65 ter number, which is 5413 -- I'm sorry, 4002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it was on the list of the documents which the Prosecution intended to tender. I therefore suggest that 65 ter 5413 will be assigned a P number at this moment. It is then in evidence. And Madam Registrar, 65 ter 5413, an ECMM Knin daily report, dated the 2nd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. I thought it was 4002, I think is the number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I made -- oh, yes, I read up till the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry, 4002 is the ECMM Knin daily report dated the 5th of August, 1995. Madam Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number P825.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P825 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, under 2a you write: "Needless to say, RSK south-western parts have now ceased to exist. Both military and civilian leaders seem to have fled before the fighting started 4 August." Can you tell us what information you had about that, about leaders fleeing before the fighting started?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 5 August, at that time, in the afternoon, we have had time to -- to talk with people who had tried to get in touch with military and civilian RSK leaders. Apparently they were not there in the RSK headquarters. So the basis was the colleagues and the fellow organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if you could go to the next page, please. If could you go to the next page, please. Under 5 a, it says: "After the shelling, a first impression of Knin town indicates that the town is still functionable. Water, electricity and telephone system are fairly intact. Comment: This might facilitate the refugee problem." Does that accurately describe how you observed Knin on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only observed that the telephone system was working. Electricity had been sometime cut. Water piping, apparently functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Liborius, the crater analysis that you did was -- you did as part of your job as an ECMM monitor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it as part of my -- my monitoring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you testified on Monday that you were looking for good craters because you wanted the quality of the crater analysis to be as good as possible. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, what I don't understand is, if you did a -- a crater analysis, and you did it your capacity as an ECMM monitor and you were looking for good craters so that you would do a quality analysis, why isn't your crater analysis reflected in a daily report, your notebook, or your diary?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crater analysis is so-called in my perception of my job, on -- on a fairly basic -- it's a first step in a chain of observations, where you would, in the RC Knin daily report as the one we have here, only be asked to produce a fairly -- you would compile a lot of information, condense it, and transmit it on. If we had a system where we should include in our reporting and in our notebook every single observation, we would have filled libraries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you understand that the Prosecution here is using that -- the results of the crater analysis you say you did in order to demonstrate shell fire from HV positions into a residential area where you say you found these craters. Do you understand that that's the purpose?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of the crater analysis was also just to get a closer feel. Everybody understood that there had been fire. I mean, it was like proving that the sun was shining today. Excuse me. It was a statement to the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But there's a reason, then, that would you go out and do a crater analysis even if it was obvious you still wanted to --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes you -- oh, sorry. Sometimes you just want a further input to your monitoring activity, and the monitors in the field would decide how that should best be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Liborius, I'm going to show you again a whole series of documents to describe sort of the -- some of the important issues on these specific dates concerning shelling, and then I will ask you a few questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I have a video first that I'd like to show the witness which is 1D50-0177.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, this is a video - and I believe transcripts have been given to the booths. This a press conference by Carl Bildt. You recall that Carl Bildt was the senior European Union negotiator for the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is in Geneva on the 6th of August after -- just for the record this is a press conference in Geneva after a meeting with the Croatian foreign minister, and we can play the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "We have a very strong position on any sort of military activity that goes against the innocent civilians and the shelling of cities is among those, and the shelling of Knin, I think, is a very, very grave thing. And I've said to them that if they want to have that clarified, the legal position of that, if they are interested in it it should be taken to the Court to judge whether that was in conformity with the -- with the laws of war that are there on not. And they answered and said that it was not a matter for individual governments to bring that up but that the Court was free to take it up and I took that as -- that they were prepared to accept a verdict from the International Court concerning the shelling of Knin."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if I should tender them as we go along. If there's no objection I would tender them right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, video and transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number D745, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D745 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the next video is again of Mr. Bildt. It is 1D50-0184. It is from the 7th of August on the BBC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "I don't think anyone was really tired [sic]. That's the problem. When you do as was done in May concerning Zagreb and you have sent a rocket in the general direction of Zagreb, you can never be certain where it hits and it happened to hit civilians. And when you do the kind of artillery shelling that we've seen in Sarajevo and that we've seen now in Knin very extensively at the beginning of the offensive, I mean, it is bound to be something that goes against civilian targets. And that is something that I think the international community must react against."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number D746.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D746 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 1D50-0187.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any technical problem that we do not see the -- there we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, this is a letter --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have some interference at this moment. I don't know where it comes from. Can you hear me, Mr. Liborius?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can hear you through a lot of noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Still good enough to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will say if I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will ask the technicians to assist us, but, at the same time, we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, this is a letter from the Croatian foreign minister and the last page on the signature line has the date, which is 8 August 1995. It is to Jacques Santer. If we can go to the last page of the document, please. The Croatian foreign minister wrote: "I must inform you that the activities and especially Mr. Bildt's recent public pronouncements have been received with the deepest regret and dismay by the government of the Republic of Croatia and Croatian public opinion in general. At its meeting on August 7, 1995, the government of Croatia concluded that Mr. Carl Bildt, as far as the Republic of Croatia is concerned, has lost credibility for continuing mediating efforts, in search for a peaceful solution to the conflict in southeastern Europe and therefore finds it impossible to cooperate with the ICF mediator as the representative of the European Union."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this letter into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number D747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D747 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Finally, Madam Registrar, 1D50-0185. If we can scroll to the bottom, please. No, that's not it, I'm sorry. That's the wrong one. Just one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Liborius, I guess I'll have to find it later. It is an ECMM report, I believe of the 9th of August, mentioning this conflict between Croatia and Mr. Bildt, over his comments. My questions for you are, you are the -- an ECMM monitor in the field, the European Union's chief mediator is in a serious diplomatic incident, I don't know what the proper diplomatic categorisation of it is. You find evidence of shelling from HV positions in Bosnia around the ECMM building in a residential area. My question to you, sir, is: Do you know of any written contemporaneous evidence of the crater analysis that you did?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the word "contemporaneous."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Within two weeks of, let's say, the 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crater analysis, as a means to support the shelling, was not required at that time. I took it that the beginning of your sentence referred to Mr. Carl Bildt's, the foundation for his words did not require any detailed crater analysis at that point in time. They were inside the UN Sector South headquarters, as he had his first press conference. It doesn't really take a crater analysis to assess whether the shelling is intense or if it is laid out all over the town. So I'm not sure that I understand the link between Carl Bildt and the crater analysis here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you the first question and it should be a relatively simple answer; it should be yes or no. Are you aware of any written document between roughly, let's say, 4 August to 31 August, which contains the results of your crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My specific crater analysis would not be tendered into ECMM documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the answer is no?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They form the very basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, let's be -- the only thing Mr. Misetic wants to know is whether the results of your crater analysis are found in any report that was made at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, shelling from north-east.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that is the result of the crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The results of your crater analysis understood as, this is what I saw, I found 61 degrees, 63 degrees, such, whether, not as an overall view but the specific results of that crater analysis of that craters, whether that appears anywhere in reports made at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that specific time just around the 4, 5, 6, August, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any later anywhere where we found these figures that were the results of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did a review of different shelling craters and we handed it over to the RC Zagreb. I believe it was in the end of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will assume, Your Honour, that the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You just answered, "We did a review of different shelling craters and we handed it over to the RC Zagreb." When else did you do reviews of shelling craters and did you provide written reports of those?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that there -- I at one time handed in notes to RC Zagreb of different -- an analysis of different shelters -- different craters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you write such a report that contained the results of crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the degrees, but where the shelling came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you -- have you ever seen a copy of that document in -- from 1995 to the present?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Liborius, I'd like to take you now to a different topic, which is your 2005 witness statement. It's P801 -- I'm sorry, let me do one additional thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 1D50-0174, while we're on the topic of crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, from your notebook I saw an entry on the 25th of October that you had a meeting with ICTY OTP investigators whom I believe were Joakim Robertsson and Jul Hansen. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 25 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the entry say again?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says meeting with -- Have you found the entry for 25 October?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I asked you because I don't know if you confused it with the 2nd of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in which document do you find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have it, I'm sorry, 25 October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I have it. If we can put it on the screen first for him. It's 1D50 -- I'm sorry, it was a P [sic] number already. D743. Now, if we can go to --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it in the meantime, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 0087 of this.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a different book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: D744, please. I apologise. There we go.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 25 October.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: ICTY investigating events, recent Storm investigation. Correct? It talks about searching responsible command structure, HV, special police, now collect evidence, have they witnessed victims, ICTY developed a questionnaire. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, this is a meeting that you had with Joakim Robertsson, an OTP investigator. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this is a meeting you held with OTP investigator two days before you met with General Gotovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Search my notebook ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, I think we established through Mr. Waespi --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- yes, the 27th is when --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- you met -- you and Mr. Gambotti met with General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Two days prior to that meeting you had already sat down with OTP investigators. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this questionnaire that is in your notes, I'd like to turn your attention back to the exhibit that was on the screen, which is 1D50-0174.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can just scroll through it a little bit. Let say at the fourth bullet point: "(Was there a lot of women and children, was the residential areas occupied.)" The next bullet says: "Was there a lot of soldiers in town? If yes, when and why were they there? Rotation." The next bullet point: "Description of the attack on Knin, where the shelling took place, residential areas, Knin hospital or other protected installations. Type of weapons used, MR LS." Mr. Waespi is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see he is on his feet but I thought he was waiting until the question would be put to the witness. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Is that the questionnaire that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What's the foundation to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I got it from Alan Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, but is that the questionnaires which is referenced --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I was going to get to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what, perhaps, Mr. Misetic wanted to ask. Therefore, Mr. Waespi, if -- if we wait until the question is put to the witness then there's still time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing is the face of the document might be helpful for the witness to start with, have you seen the document before going to Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm walking him through it is to see if he is familiar with the various portions of it but ... If we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The top category says: "Description about how the Croats should have been able before and during the attack to monitor the situation and take steps to prevent possible war crimes being committed - on all levels; from the ground forces to the supreme CO of HV," and then it lists the various methods. And then if we could go to the final page, please. If we could scroll to the bottom. And there's a note that says: "If you do not know, do not guess. It is bullet points, so please feel free to describe the facts as you wish (maybe in form of a letter) and do not answer the questions on this questionnaire by referring to the above order." And then it has the ICTY investigators on the bottom. Is this the questionnaire that you're referring to in your notes that was given to you as a basis to prepare your first witness statement in this case, sir?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall having seen that questionnaire before. The reference in my notebook, ICTY developed a questionnaire, was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, first before you answer that, if I could just call your attention to refresh your recollection a bit. The first page of your first witness statement. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's the cover letter that you sent back on the 13th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, you're writing to Mr. Hansen and Mr. Robertsson and the reference is: "A, our conversation in Knin on 2 November 1995; and B, ICTY questionnaire from October 1995." Now, was that the questionnaire that you used as a template to prepare the first witness statement you did in this case?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first witness statement was prepared as a chronological expression of my observations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why the reference to the ICTY questionnaire on the cover letter?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the ICTY developed a questionnaire reference originated from my notebook here. I haven't had the questionnaire in front of me when I did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a copy of that questionnaire, however?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have it in front of me, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the question, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Did I receive a copy? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question was not whether it was in front of you, you had said that already. The question then was whether you had received it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You never received a questionnaire --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- prepared by the ICTY. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: However the probative value may be, Your Honour, I still tender that questionnaire into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, work product of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, if Alan Tieger gave it to Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not object. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I would like to talk to my colleague before I give my final assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First of all, I mean, it is not work product if it is given to third parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Of course, I was not to be taken really serious at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's his fault. He made me say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll take the rap.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The -- I guess we would put on the record if that is not the questionnaire and appears that there is a reference to the questionnaire and if the OTP knows that there is another one that was given to him that it be produced to us in its place, in the place of this one. This is the only one I have been given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll give Mr. Waespi time to consult with Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it could be marked for identification meanwhile. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number D748, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May we hear from you by tomorrow, Mr. Waespi. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Madam Registrar, can we go to P801, please. If we can go to page 5 in the English, please. All the way at the bottom, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to read this portion to you. "On some occasions I interviewed HV soldiers and asked them why they were doing this. The soldiers explained that the looting was their reward for participating in the operation, as they were lowly paid, and it was considered as part of their wages. They said that their senior commanders had specifically authorised them to help themselves to the goods. When asked about the destruction, the killing of livestock, and the poisoning of the wells, they explained that this was to prevent the Serbs from returning. I understood exactly what they were saying because I come from a farming background and to destroy the infrastructure and destroy the means of their livelihood would ensure that no one could return and live in that particular region."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could now turn to P802, please. At the bottom of the page in English, on page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'll read this to you: "On page 5 of my 2005 statement, I refer to being told by HV soldiers that they had been authorised by their commanders to loot. I remember that I was told on three occasions by different HV soldiers, the first being on the 7th of August at the old RC Knin building. The soldier I spoke to was a Home Guard soldier. I know that because he told me he was a member of the Home Guard, and I saw the insignia for the Home Guard on his uniform. In my report of the 7th of August, I referred to the 7th and 4th Guards Brigade soldiers looting. There were two 7th Guards Brigade soldiers with us when I spoke to the Home Guard soldier. Later that same day, I encountered three soldiers from the 4th Guards Brigade who were just arriving at my own accommodation and when I spoke to them, one of them said it was their right to collect things they wanted." And then you talk about the third occasion being later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to P805, please. If we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You see this is the report co-authored by you and Mr. Bigland?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, please. I'm sorry, the previous page, I apologise, at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of the sitrep -- sorry, the daily report, on the day that you say on two separate occasions that HV soldiers told you that they had been authorised by their highest commanders to take war booty because it was part of their wages, you and Mr. Bigland write a report that says: "In the Knin area, it seems as if random looting and destruction of houses and property is about to reach a degree where it will get even more difficult to restart normal life here. Comment: It is very unlikely that this is a deliberate policy of the authorities. It is more likely that, as the front-line, more disciplined troops are moving out, the second-line soldiers are less disciplined and more ready to grab what ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page. "... they can."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Liborius, you would agree with me that an ECMM monitor being told by Croatian troops in Knin on the 7th, that they had authorisation to take property because it is part of their wages is an important fact?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: A fact important enough that an ECMM monitor would be required to report such information in a daily report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, not only is it not only in the daily report, sir, but the comment at the end is exactly the opposite. Is it not? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you go to the top of the report, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I said the comment at the end. Let's talk about -- the comment at the end is a conclusion that is directly contradicted by what you say you were told on the 7th but HV soldiers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we go to the previous page at the bottom, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would you -- let me ask the question a different way. Would you agree with me that if HV soldiers told you that they had received authorisation from their highest command to go ahead and loot, that that would be inconsistent with a comment that it is very unlikely that this is a deliberate policy of the authorities. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I didn't write that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So there was a failure to communicate between you and Mr. Bigland. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had signed off the report, the last line would not have read like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it typical that your name would be on the author line of a report that you hadn't reviewed before it went out?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The RC Knin daily report, at that time, was, as I said yesterday or the day before, the work of different people, so it would not be inconsistent with what you suggest there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The question is very specific: Was it typical for your name to be on the author line of a report that you hadn't reviewed before it went out? Regardless of where the sources of information are, do you review the reports before you send them up?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly became aware that there was a need for consolidated views on the report. This is one of the examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask for an instruction that the witness answer the question as posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me read it. I may have another little problem, Mr. -- let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question was whether that -- I take, it often happened that you being the co-author of a report would let it send out without you having reviewed it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did not happen often. But it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just an observation. The question was actually a compound question. There were two different questions in one. The witness just answered to the best of his capabilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Liborius, did you review this report before it was sent out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not in its final stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Because that was implied in your question. As a matter of fact, I was checking whether that assumption was already in the evidence, yes or not. That was --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I wanted the first -- the general policy and then I was going ask the specifics with respect to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, given that you and I agree that that is an important fact for whatever reason your finding didn't make it into the 7th of August daily report, so you must have made sure that it got into the 8th of August daily report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can show me the 8th of August report. It certainly made it into the way of the subsequent reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I can show you that report. What I'm asking you is very simple. Do you believe there is a report on the 8th of August, where it is reported that you were told by HV soldiers that their commanders had authorised them to loot? Is that in the report for the 8th of August, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I prefer to see the 8th of August -- if we're discussing text here I really prefer to see the 8th of August report here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is P806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Either the witness remembers, then he can ask the question and apparently what he tell us is that I would have to check in the report because I have no clear recollection of whether it is or is not. And that's fair. So then I leave it up to you whether you want to put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you don't know, as we sit here, without looking at a document whether you put it in a daily report or not. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, it is on the screen now. We can scroll through it.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does that refresh your recollection? Did you report it in the 8th of August daily report?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reference to looting is certainly there. It is again a report written by Mr. Bigland and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the question whether the words "they have been authorised to loot" is in the report, I did not find that here. So, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. One question to end this area, sir. The house you were actually living in, it was owned by someone named Mr. Urukalo who had actually been a mobilised ARSK soldier prior to Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was owned by the woman, but Urukalo, yes, family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, in your diary you note that on the 1st of August the husband had just come back from the front line. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So the house you were in was the house of a front line soldier?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was seldom home. So I mainly met the housewife and the daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, your diary, I believe, and can you just tell me if you know this or not, he was on the front line?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what I was told, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's a good time for a break. We will have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, Prosecution has no objection for D748, MFI, to come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D748 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, following up on that topic we ended with before the break, who from the ECMM was with you when these Croatian soldiers made these statements that they had been authorised to loot?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was alone when I encountered the soldiers in my own accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And without going through all the documents now, I'm just asking you for your own recollection as you sit here, do you recall any document ever, while you were part of the ECMM in Croatia, where you as part of a daily report or your 100-day report or any other report, reported that it had been reported to you by Croatian soldiers that they were authorised to loot? Do you have any recollection of any such document?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the issue that the soldiers said they were authorised to loot, yes, it was brought up in some of the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which ones, that can you recall?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember at this point in time. I will have to see the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, do you have 100-day report, a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will ask you, whatever reports you have, your 100-day report, tonight as you're reviewing things, and tomorrow preparing for the session, to go through them and see if you can find a reference to such an admission, okay?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can do my best. But I don't have the entire ECMM library at my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: True. Just -- but whatever you need to refresh your recollection, or whatever you have. I'm reminded to ask you: You said you were alone when you encountered in your accommodation. I also testified that this happened at the old RC Knin building. Who was with you at the old RC Knin building when these soldiers told you this?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My team colleague, Eric Hendriks. We had a tour through the RC Knin house, and we went -- it was a quite large compound, so we went through the facility, and I believe that Eric Hendriks was with us in the -- one of the large rooms on the top floor. We later saw the soldiers out in the field around the RC again, and I believe that Eric Hendriks was also with me at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Hendriks was there when these soldiers told you this?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And with regard to, I believe, your last question ... Did you ask for the third reference as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, just those two. But if there's a third reference where you were told that they were authorised to loot by their senior commanders, I would like you to tell us when and who was with you.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third instance where we encountered soldiers that said that it was their right to take over property was at the -- the new ECMM house --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the colleagues of the team was my Greek colleague --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, I'm going to stop you there. We're talking about apples and orange there, aren't we? That was a dispute over who had the right to use that piece of property. That wasn't an issue of looting property that was in the building. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, what you were talking about is the dispute with the CALOs that we went through earlier in your diary about the use of the RC Knin -- the old RC Knin building. Is that the general topic that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just make sure. You asked me who were in my company when I had a chance to hear Croatian soldiers saying that it was their right to loot and take over property, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific because I don't want to have a broad question which is unclear. You testified that soldiers told you that they were authorised to loot because it was part of their wages. Now, the third time, did soldiers tell you that part of their wages was that they could loot?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third time the soldiers told me and my team colleagues that they had the right to take over the property in order -- but it was not -- the wage question was in the first instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'm going to move to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't know if the Bench want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about your meeting with General Gotovina on the 25th and the days preceding. Now, we've established that you met with the ICTY investigators on the 25th. From your first witness statement there's also a reference in the cover letter to a second meeting with them on the 2nd of November, 1995. And in between that week, those two meetings, is exactly the -- the 27th, when you and Mr. Gambotti met with General Gotovina. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's talk -- first, this morning you discussed that you had another meeting, you believe, on the 23rd with General Gotovina and I believe you called him Mr. Selic. Is that right? It is actually Mr. Zelic, okay?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could pull up 1D50-0178, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now a document the cover page is in Croatian. And if we could flip to the next page, please. And there's a -- first let's -- let's look at the cover page together. This is forwarded to General Gotovina on the 22nd. And it says: "Today, on 22 October 1995 ... the office received a letter from ECMM office Knin, requesting that we set up a meeting for the future chief of the Regional Centre of the ECMM Zagreb, Mr. Gambotti, with the commander of the Military District, General Gotovina. "The said individual requests a meeting with you on 27 October, possibly at noon or earlier." Now, if you look at the original, inserted there it says "da," to the right, in the middle of the page it says "petak," which means Friday, and then it says [B/C/S spoken] at 10.00 a.m. And if we could flip to the next page, please. Now, this is the letter you sent on the 22nd requesting a meeting with General Gotovina. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, you didn't meet with General Gotovina on the 22nd or 23rd. What you were doing was making notes of your communications to schedule the meeting with General Gotovina. And if we turn to your notebook, D744, page 6, please. Now, if we look to the right-hand side of the page it says 10.00, Pasic, General Gotovina, Mr. Pupovac, timing, and I believe it says slotting?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Floating.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Floating. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it -- it has not been established precisely yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you see from the cover letter and the letter that you wrote that in the handwritten notation on the Croatian version it was written Friday, 10.00 a.m., yes. And your notes, then, for the next day, on the 23rd, say at 10.00 there's a meeting with General Gotovina. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: There would have been no need for you to go through the CALOs to schedule a meeting to send a letter to General Gotovina if in fact you had met with him personally and could have asked for that meeting face to face. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- you asked for this particular meeting, because it would inquire -- it would entail a quite detailed agenda and the HRC designate. That would be a long meeting, not like a usual meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'm saying is, sir, is that you're trying to interpret your notes today, and what I'm suggesting to you is what your notes are referring to is your effort on the 22nd and 23rd to schedule a meeting with General Gotovina for the 27th with Mr. Gambotti. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And all else, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the document 1D50-0178, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number D749.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D749 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now we looked at your notes for the 25th earlier where, amongst other things in the notations of your meeting with the OTP investigators, it was discussed command structure -- if we could flip forward a few pages here. I believe it's on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we get to the 25th of October, please, so ... there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, it looks -- on the right it says: "Investigate way." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Investigate event."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Event. Okay. What's the next line say?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Recent Storm." And then "investigate" and then "way."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then after that?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Collect documents and papers, search, responsible." It says, "until now."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command structure HV special police. Then, now collect evidence, have they witnessed? Victims are searched. Ten persons witness themselves. All lead to witnesses. And I believe that this is a description of what has been going on for the ICTY so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you complete that page so that we're sure what it says?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: ICTY developed a questionnaire what happened in restriction of movement days, what happened after. How to identify perpetrators, HV plates, units. Suggests, Rick Bigland during and then questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the notebook that you kept, you used this notebook to assist you in preparing your daily reports. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could turn it that daily report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think Mr. Waespi used this document, but we haven't recorded a P number for the 28th October daily report. I don't know if it's our error or ... It is 65 ter 4337 -- sorry P822, I'm told. If we could turn the page, please. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "Asked about lessons learned in OPS Storm: Both positive and negative. The latter being the lack of control with 'undisciplined soldiers of non-professional units doing extraordinary things. The General stated that the HV lacked, and still lack, the level of skilled NCOs and medium-level commanders able to control the soldiers." Now, if we turn to your notes, and I believe -- this is P821, I believe. And I'd ask to you pay attention to the fact that when you prepared your daily report and you saw the word "extraordinary" in that report, it says that "extraordinary" refers to undisciplined soldiers of non-professional units doing extraordinary things. So you actually included the word "extraordinary" in quotation marks in the daily report. Do you see that? Actually we've --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We lost the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me take you here, if we could ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll through this, please. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I prefer to use the original, so if we could go to D744, please. And it's page 18 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, if we can scroll down there now. In the original it says: "Professional soldiers were controlled the --" can you tell us what that word is?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much improved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The much improved extraordinary ...

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extraordinate [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Meaning extraordinary in English?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, that is the only time the word "extraordinary" appears in your notebook. Is that correct? For that day, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in 16, in view of the next page. There is also --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll stand corrected. If -- in this discussion about discipline, that's the only time the word "extraordinary" appears. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it also on 16. If look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we go through the context or the logical progression of the discussion here, in that discussion, where you referred to as the silent conversation between Gambotti and Gotovina --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- the word "extraordinary" appears once. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now when you wrote your daily report, for the 27th and the 28th, you used that word and put it in General Gotovina's mouth as him saying: "The General stated undisciplined soldiers of non-professional units doing extraordinary things." And then you continued on by saying: "But all the professional units are still kept free from these accusations despite the fact that numerous IO have witnessed such events involving professional units." That's in the daily report that you prepared. So what I am again putting to you, sir, there was no silent admission by General Gotovina when you wrote that report on the 28th. In fact, would you agree with me that you wrote quite the opposite, that General Gotovina continued to keep the professional units free from those types of accusations. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I wanted to say, as before, that Gambotti and I carefully discussed the way the meeting went and how it should be reflected in the report. That's what you have in the report there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that you and Mr. Gambotti provided a report that was inaccurate in terms of what took place in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a consolidated effort of the two of us. And if you read the report, if we could it have it up again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. P822, please. And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you read the report, "undisciplined soldiers of a non-professional units doing extraordinary things," that was the closest to the quotation I could come together with Gambotti. Then the team comment, starting: "TC: Tailored to the presence of the HRC designate that in our view promoted postwar image --" Sorry. Speak -- slow down. "Speaking a lot about the role of the HV in a peaceful society. Unlike previous meetings, the General now admitted that a lot of atrocities were committed in Storm. But all the professional units are kept free from these accusations, despite the fact that numerous IOs have witnessed such events involving professional units. The lack of skilled NCOs and medium-level commanders is maybe the understatement of the month." That was as both the HRC designate and I felt that we could -- could take it at that point. Now what does that mean? It means that the HRC designate, of course, had also interpreted the silence as in fact an admission. Now, he would later, in the further reporting in the ECMM structure reflect his impressions. So I do not see any -- dealing as you would suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood the answer, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try -- if you don't understand the question, Mr. Liborius, I would invite you to tell us rather than to give an incomprehensible answer for Mr. Misetic to a question you did not understand. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You've come here to testify that there was a silent conversation, whatever that may mean, between Mr. Gambotti and General Gotovina, where General Gotovina silently admitted that professional forces of the HV were involved in atrocities. Is that -- have I fairly stated what you stated in the course of your testimony thus far?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You write a report on the 28th where you write: "But all the professional units are still kept free from these accusations." And I put it to you again, that what you've told us here, about a silent admission by General Gotovina, is inconsistent with what you wrote in the report on the 28th. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I -- I'm afraid that the full understanding is perhaps missed. But at this point in time, yes. But if the, Judge, Your Honour, you require me to -- to elaborate further, I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I first want a clear answer to the question, the question being that where you testified about a silent conversation apparently interpreted as an admission, that your report, as Mr. Misetic puts it to you, says otherwise, is inconsistent with that testimony. Could you answer that question, to start with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The report itself, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that it's an answer to a question you understood, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it is important that also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just there's no question about that. Okay. Now would you like -- apparently you feel the need to give a further explanation. If you want to give a brief explanation, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have no problem with that. I do want to state and advise the witness that the longer we go into long explanations, the longer the examination goes. But feel free to clarify on this particular point, but just keep it in mind for future questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm prepared to continue next week on videolink if that is required. It is important to understand the reporting structure of the ECMM, that the RC Knin reports is only one and that the HRC would, in his further work in the headquarters with his information gathered, work on. So the RC Knin report is only one part. And I'm sure that the HRC designate had his impressions that there was this admission. But, at that time, it was a very sensitive subject, of course, and that it was perhaps best that that be reflected in subsequent reports made at the headquarter level. Thank you. The reflection is: "But all the professional units are kept free from these accusations." What I said before was that the General was walking a fine line between the official position and then the -- the acknowledgment that the HRC designate, Mr. Gambotti, was in fact right. Now, that would of course require further conversations, if you wish. Because it was a change of, so to speak, a policy of how you related to the campaign by the Croatian authorities at that time then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see. Now, I'm the one who might not have understood all of your answer. Mr. Liborius, the beginning of your answer let's focus on that. You say it is it important to understand that the HRC might have further elaborated on the information gathered. So I understand this to be that even if the report is not consistent with your testimony, that others might have added something to that. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The HRC used this meeting as one of the events, one of the meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to understand that. From what I see, this report is authored by you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you telling us that although you authored it, that someone, some of your superiors, has instructed you to add something or -- how do I have to understand this reference to your superior, the -- from what I understand, the head to add something in a report you authored?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said previously, that we discussed how to reflect the meeting, Mr. Gambotti and I, in the afternoon after the meeting, knowing that he would, in his further work in the headquarter level, be able to develop some of the points in, among other things, also the question of extraordinary events by professional soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what you meant when you said: "The lack of skilled NCOs and medium-level commanders is maybe the understatement of the month."

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By that I mean that if you attribute all the destruction, looting and burning and so on, to the sentence, well, we lacked the skilled NCOs and medium-level commanders, that is a very, very ironically short way of saying that this is a reason for all our problems. That the General stated that we lacked the NCOs and medium-level commanders explains everything that went on after Operation Storm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is like saying we failed to understand that there was an earthquake coming. It just came.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, when did the Croatian army form its first NCO school?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I have in my notebook as General Gotovina said, We have created NCO centre that has worked for two years. I don't know whether a NCO school has been there before. That was what the General told us at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you check to see if there was NCO training that had taken place for longer than two years?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not feel the need at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you ever look to see how many trained NCOs the Croatian army had?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to ask one additional question in this respect. You said that the reporting, after having discussed the matter - and let me just check your answer - you said the -- Mr. Gambotti would in his further work in the headquarter level be able to develop some of the points in, among other things, also the question of extraordinary events by professional soldiers. Now, the report, unlike your testimony, may admit that extraordinary events may have taken place, but not by professional soldiers. Could you explain to me why saying that it was not done by professional soldiers would enable Mr. Gambotti to develop some of the points in the question of extraordinary events by professional soldiers? Because the report says that it was not these professional soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The team comment, beginning "tailored to the present" and so on, was the result of a conversation between Mr. Gambotti and I. We discussed, in particular also this next sentence: "But all the professional soldiers are kept free from these accusations." Mr. Gambotti had the feeling that the General, having deployed both the official line and also silently had admitted to his questions that wasn't it right that extraordinary events that were also committed by professional soldiers, both of them were deployed in the conversation, but that the admittance part of professional soldiers, it was the first time it was heard, and it would require further investigation, if you wish. So we decided the formulation carefully like you see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you heard for the first time what was said in a silent conversation. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you should take into consideration that the two gentlemen had a conversation in French, tete-a-tete, prior to the formal part of the meeting. And as they both have a, so to speak, French background, they developed a good rapport between the two. The conversation was quite long. When we reached point 15, as I said before, there was a -- a good dynamic, ping-pong dynamic in the conversation, and the silent part of the acknowledgment was interpreted by both Mr. Gambotti and myself as a yes answer to the -- the gist of that particular subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you said you heard that for the first time ... it would require further investigation. Now, is by not reporting it, is that furthering an investigation or was the investigation in any other way developed or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HRC preferred that we should -- that he should further the pursuit of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you know how he did that? Have you any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just one question on that, sir. If that's true what you're saying now, wouldn't you have just -- if there was any doubt about the fact that General Gotovina kept professional units free from these accusations, wouldn't you have just not written that sentence?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sentence was the product, the conclusion of Mr. Gambotti's and my conversation, how that should be reflected. So -- so the question is answered no, I wouldn't write it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's clear this up. So what you are really saying is you and Mr. Gambotti afterwards agreed to write a sentence that you both felt wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deploying both one line, the official line and then the silent admittance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, people are supposed to read this up your information chain. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was supposed to read it. He is the HRC designate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As well as other people, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but primarily he.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So he is writing to himself?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, the HRC receives the RC reports -- the team reports. That was the reason why that this sensitive subject should be developed further and he felt perfectly capable of doing that because he was in the chain of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, the memo line says you're sending it to CC Split and it says for information to RC Zagreb. So you are actually distributing this beyond you and Mr. Gambotti writing a private little memorandum to each other?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If could you go to the top, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sure, let's go to the first page.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There you see it is inside the RC Zagreb structure. It is inside the HRC structure. CC Split is a coordination centre subordinated to the Regional Centre Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My point is you're sending it to more than just Mr. Gambotti?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
