utterances.text: And according to you, you and Mr. Gambotti decided to send false information in a written report to people within the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omit the word "false," please. It's not -- it's the truth but not the whole truth. And the HRC would be perfectly capable of knowing what is going on inside the RC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And other people who go this report wouldn't have been able to know of silent conversations and silent admissions, correct?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, there would be follow-on meetings inside the RC with the other members where we could meet to discuss our findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it would be there that would you say, Listen, where we wrote that all professional units were kept free from these accusations, what we meant was no, he actually admitted it.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to appreciate the full answer, and with the risk of repeating myself, if you deploy both the official line and you say, well, not really. You can have that dialectic difference. I know it's a very tricky issue and of course it goes to the core.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Liborius.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I do have to ask a question as my colleague reminds me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many times in your reports did you not tell the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It was the only meeting, is that what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President. I object that's not what the witness said --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He says it was not the whole truth in his report. It is exactly what he said. "Omit the word 'false,' please. It is the truth and not the whole truth."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question again for the witness is: How many times in your daily reports did you not write the whole truth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, let's try to avoid a semantic discussion on whether not the whole truth still is the truth. That's -- it -- It appears from your testimony, Mr. Liborius, that in this report not the whole of the truth was reflected and now Mr. Misetic asks you how often this happened in reports you authored.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the only example I can recall now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if I could have -- this is one of the videos that went in yesterday. We will play it on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before we play it, Mr. Liborius, this is a portion of the video you did with the OTP in 1997. Now I'm going to play you two minutes of the clip. This is the portion where you went to Kricke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Kricke. It's in the Drnis area. And I'd like you to -- after you watch the video what I'm going to ask you to do is help the Trial Chamber to determine which houses that are burned are owned by a Croat, which houses were owned by a Serb and whether the damage was done before Operation Storm or after Operation Storm. First can you tell me before we play the video when you were doing these patrols, how were you able to determine whether a particular village was burned down before or after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have information from our usual patrols before Operation Storm to relate to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you saw a house that had been burned down on the spot, would you be able to say -- assuming it is not still on fire. Let's say if the fire ended and it is now two weeks after the fire has been put out. How would you tell that that house had been burned down two weeks ago as opposed to a year ago?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ECMM information on the villages, houses there, was quite detailed. It was very, very, very, seldom that houses or hamlets would be burned down in the RSK period. I cannot recall of a village burning just, say, a half a year before Operation Storm. It was a so-called state, semi-state RSK. In our usual patrols through the area, we would have that information to relate to when we saw destruction afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How would you know --

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How would you know whether a village was majority Croat or majority Serb?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, from our previous information, before Operation Storm, the Regional Centre Knin with its ECMM teams had throughout the war, covered the whole area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's play the video. It is from the 58 minute 58 second mark of P821 to the 1 minute and 56 second mark of P821.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Liborius, I would ask you to pay particular attention to how do you know it is a Serb or Croat house and how do you know when the damage took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Unknown Male: ... May 1997. We are in the Drnis area south-east of the Drnis in the village Kricke and we follow the road towards south-east."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, you see that that is Kricke?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us how when you were in the theatre in August of 1995 as well as on this patrol in 1997, how were you able to first identify it as a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's still a noise here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that those who are -- there is still a volume button on it and perhaps if we stop playing. There we are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your question how we would know whether it was a Serb or a Croat-dominated village, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually we would relate to the information that was gathered by the teams prior to Operation Storm. Secondly, we would relate to the government of Croatia's statistics survey for each municipality, the big blue book on municipality structures. Secondly, whether it was a Croat or a Serb-owned house, was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would always myself hesitate to say a Serb or a Croat-owned house. I don't do that in my report. Usually when coming to an area after Operation Storm, where there were inhabitants, I would ask who owned this house. Generally some of the houses would have a sign saying Croatian house. That would be the sign that some of the houses had been taken over by some Croats. With regard to your question how to establish when the damage was done, that would usually require us to be in the area close to the houses, see if there were recent traces of burnings, see if there were traces of battle damage, trees around the area, fences being demolished by shrapnels, to inspect, so to speak, the way the damage was inflicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you were just driving through a village without stopping and you see burned out villages, how do you know, again, taking aside the situation where the village or the houses are smouldering still, but just looking at what we looked at on the video there, how would you know if you were just driving through that it was a Serb village as opposed to a Croat village and that was destroyed Operation Storm as opposed to before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as I said, if I had patrolled or my team or colleagues had patrolled in that area prior to Operation Storm, and most of the area was -- was patrolled through many times, month and weeks prior to Operation Storm, so there was an updated accurate knowledge of the level of destruction prior to Operation Storm. Now you come through a village, start of July, it is not destroyed. You come to a village mid-August, destroyed. So you -- you relate to your prior ECMM-gathered information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I would like to call up again a document that the Prosecution tendered right at the end of the direct. I have it still under the 65 ter which is 65 ter 4350, which is Mr. Liborius' 100-day report of 21 November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Liborius, looking at that video, could you tell anything from that video, as to when the damage occurred?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not participating, myself, in that particular trip, as it was mentioned yesterday, to Drnis area. If you would re-wind the tape, I would give some indications. Now, I'm very hesitant on second-guessing from a video; I prefer being there in person. First observation. Second observation. Drnis, as we knew it, became a part of the RSK due to a problem of the pink zones, the army of RSK. So, again, we would relate to the information gathered by monitoring prior to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, before we start with a new subject, I'm looking at the clock. Perhaps we should spend two or three minutes or further discussing scheduling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I just wrap this up quickly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I just need to go to -- what the Bates number on the bottom is 388731, which is ... it should be, I think, 43 pages in, if I'm not mistaken. That's not -- I'm sorry. The Bates number is 388731. We're about 50 pages off now. Page 44 of the document. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you look that line and you find Kricke, this is the UNMO report you attached to your own 100-day report. Now, the UNMO report says: "Kricke," with the coordinates -- and I have checked the coordinates so they're the same as what was played on the video. It says: "Kricke damaged prior to Operation Storm." Now did you go through the videos with the Office of the Prosecutor to determine what was being represented on the videos was for sure damage that had occurred during or after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SOREN LIBORIUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went through the videos it was to ascertain whether my voice was the one on the video. I did not dwell on the question on each -- each and every hamlet that they went through, whether it was destroyed prior to Operation Storm. Now, in this particular case, it is the voice of Mr. Jul Hansen who is going through and I did not participate in that particular trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will end here but I will pick up on this subject tomorrow in light of your instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Liborius, some research was done on your travel schedule. Although there is a plane to your destination which goes later Friday evening, you would not arrive until 5.20 in the morning which might be a bit too much for you. Therefore, you were so kind to offer to say that you would continue your testimony through videolink. Now usually whether there is a videolink or not, is usually decided upon the Chamber upon application by the parties and, of course, if you would express such a wish since you are, at this moment, entitled to speak anymore with Mr. Waespi, of course, we could consider that. But we ordinarily would hear the testimony viva voce. When would you be available to come back to The Hague if you would leave on Friday evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a question I'm sorry that I cannot answer right on the spot here. My government requires my attention to a lot of details in September, and in the beginning of October. However, when I indicated a videolink, the embassy is prepared to provide that and I think it would facilitate a further discussion as the case is still fresh in mind and perhaps also be the easiest one. We have a lot of experience with detailed videolinking, so the quality is usually very good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Liborius, I'm working with videolinks so often that although I appreciate that you explain to me that it can be done with quite some good quality, my question was whether you would be available to come back The Hague and not to expound further on what you consider the advantages of videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to go back to Moscow to answer that question, Your Honour. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please get the relevant information you would need by tomorrow so that you could inform the Chamber about your availability in the very, very near future?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll see what I can do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day. And, Mr. Liborius, I again instruct you, and you know it by heart perhaps already, that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony you have given or you're still about to give. And although Madam Registrar gave me the right information about tomorrow, I'm afraid that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom I, unless it changes overnight again. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 11th day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
